subject: Human Evolution
title: The Endurance Running Hypothesis
description: One-minute skill: The Endurance Running Hypothesis.

hook.text: Humans can run for hours without stopping. Most mammals overheat and collapse after a few kilometres.

buildup.text: Bramble and Lieberman proposed that Homo evolved for endurance running—to chase prey to exhaustion.

discovery.text: Our springy Achilles tendons, sweat glands, and nuchal ligament all only make sense for running, not walking.

twist.text: No other primate can run long distances. These features appeared with Homo erectus 2 million years ago.

climax.text: Persistence hunting—running animals until they collapse—may have been our original hunting method.

punchline.text: We evolved to run prey into the ground.

quiz.question: What is persistence hunting?
options: Chasing prey until it collapses from heat exhaustion
